segments.title: 第91章 大伯駕到
segments.content:
Rekindling the Verdant Years Chapter 91 Eldest Uncle's Arrival

Yuhang City Writers' Association.

Li Guoru stood in the lounge with a cigarette dangling from his lips, a calligraphy brush in hand, his strokes flying across the Xuan paper on the table like dragons and snakes.

At sixty-three this year, he was already retired and would often come to the Writers' Association to pass the time, drinking tea, chatting, and sharing recent outstanding works with a few old friends.

Practicing calligraphy on a whim like this was also a kind of pleasure.

"Your handwriting is truly ugly." Sun Jingchun commented with a chuckle after a glance. "It has no sharp edge, and the strokes lack power. Did you skip a meal or something?"

"You talk too much." Li Guoru shot him a look, not at all angry. After decades of friendship, trading jabs and insults was commonplace. "Are you done with your work?"

"Not yet, what's the rush." Sun Jingchun tidied his thinning hair, then put on a cap for seniors. "The National Day holiday is for resting. Work can wait until after the break."

"Then why did you say you were busy just now?"

"Isn't that because there was still work left to do before the holiday?" Sun Jingchun shook his head. "Our province established an Online Writers' Association this year. It's a small temple with many affairs, but the higher-ups take it seriously, so they have to pull people from the main Writers' Association to help."

"Oh, right, I remember that." Li Guoru put down his brush and asked curiously, "So what are you busy with? Aren't these online writers just people who write stuff on the internet?"

"Well, it's National Day, so in October, another batch of online writers has applied for membership, and they all need to be reviewed." Sun Jingchun fished a pack of cigarettes from Li Guoru's pocket, pulling one out as he spoke. "Those web novel platforms also submit recommended names, and there are quite a few of them."

"So what's the verdict now?" Li Guoru lit the cigarette for him and leaned against the table to ask. "Can the stuff written online be as good as what we write?"

"Good, my ass." Sun Jingchun rolled his eyes. "It's garbage that's unreadable. Only good for fooling little kids."

"It's mainly that these people create online, they've got a lot of readers, and their influence is gradually growing."

"You don't understand this kind of thing? As long as there's influence, there's value. Whether it's good or not isn't something for us to consider."

"That makes sense." Li Guoru nodded, stubbing out his cigarette in the ashtray.

Just then, his phone rang. Li Guoru raised a hand in a gesture and then answered the call: "Hello?"

"I know, I haven't forgotten."

"Alright, you're here? I'm coming out now."

After hanging up, Li Guoru smiled and bid farewell to Sun Jingchun. "My son is here to pick me up. I'm going to my younger brother's place for dinner today, so I won't chat with you any longer."

"Sure, go ahead." Sun Jingchun waved his hand. "I'll pack up and head home too."

A little after four in the afternoon, Li Guoru's family of five drove to Jincheng Community.

When they arrived at 401, Li Guohong had been waiting for a long time and immediately welcomed them in.

"I don't think you've been here since the New Year, have you? Come, come." Li Guohong ushered Li Guoru in with a smile, then greeted his nephew, who was the same age as him.

After entering, his sister-in-law and niece-in-law went to the kitchen to help Lin Xiuhong.

Li Guohong spotted his grandnephew, who was trailing at the back, and reached out with a smile to pull him over. "You're in university this year, right? I heard you even went out of province?"

"This kid didn't do well on his exams, he went to the university of finance and economics in Changning." Li Dao said, pointing at his son. "He had a chance to get into Qianjiang University, but unfortunately, he didn't have the drive."

Li Xiang was tall and thin, holding a phone. After greeting Li Guohong in a low voice, he quietly sat down on the living room sofa and started looking at his phone by himself.

Li Guohong shook his head helplessly. "Go easy on him. What's wrong with the university of finance and economics in Changning? It's a 211 university."

"Can't I say a few words?" Li Dao was also vexed by his son's failure to live up to expectations. "He just slacked off too much before the college entrance exam, always playing games or reading those web novels. Otherwise, he definitely would have gotten into Qianjiang University."

"Alright." Li Guoru, sitting to the side, waved his hand. "A guy like you who never even went to university shouldn't be making a fuss here. No matter what, Li Xiang has the highest academic qualification in our family. Has anyone in our family ever gotten into a 211 university before?"

"There's still Li Luo," Li Dao couldn't help but say. "Li Luo got into the Affiliated No. 1 Middle School in the high school entrance exam. In my opinion, he might just be Qianjiang University material in the future."

As he spoke, Li Dao found it strange. He looked around the living room and asked, "Where's your Li Luo? Out playing?"

"Didn't we buy Third Uncle's house a while back?" Li Guohong said. "That place is closer to the Affiliated No. 1 Middle School, so we let him live there usually. He should be back soon."

"No wonder." Li Dao nodded, then walked over to his son, Li Xiang, and urged, "When Li Luo gets here, you two youngsters should talk more. Don't be so quiet all the time, got it?"

Li Xiang glanced up, then lowered his head again, making it unclear whether he had agreed.

"Speaking of which, I remember Xiuhong mentioned it to me last time." Li Guoru, now sitting on the sofa with his legs crossed, lit a cigarette. Recalling his chat with Sun Jingchun today, he couldn't help but ask, "She said your Li Luo is still writing in private?"

"Oh, right, that." Li Guohong remembered and broke into a smile. "Just a kid writing for fun. I've read it, and it's quite interesting, but it definitely can't compare to you folks in the Writers' Association."

"Eh, you can't say that." Li Guoru said with a grin. "Li Luo is still young, isn't he? He has a lot of room for improvement in the future."

"Li Luo is still writing?" Li Dao became curious as well. "What's it about?"

"Just some nonsense he writes online." Li Guohong waved his hand. "But I see that this book of his has quite a lot of readers. I don't know if it's any good."

"Writing online?" Li Dao's brow rose, and he took out his phone. "Tell me the name, I'll search for it."

"What was it called..." Li Guohong also frowned, taking out his phone to check. "I'm Really Not a Star, that's it."

As soon as he said this, the others had no reaction, but Li Xiang, who was sitting in the corner, suddenly lifted his head and blinked. His originally sullen expression instantly came to life.

But no one else noticed.

Li Dao searched for it on his phone.

Li Guoru directly took Li Guohong's phone and glanced at it. "Oh, online novels. I know about these."

"Yo, it even has a Baike encyclopedia entry?" Li Dao was a little surprised. "Not bad."

"Let's see what it's about." Li Guoru raised an eyebrow, tapped on the first chapter, and began to read with a serious air.

Soon, however, his brows furrowed. What on earth is this? he thought.

Something about being reborn, a pop queen's concert, and some 'system' or whatever. What kind of mess was this?

Li Guoru had never encountered this kind of work before and was instantly baffled.

And just at that moment.

A sound came from the entrance.

Li Luo pushed the door open from outside. Seeing the people sitting on the living room sofa, he froze for a moment.

"What are you standing there for?" Seeing Li Luo, Li Guohong immediately waved him over. "Your eldest uncle and his family are here for dinner. They're all reading your work. Come over and listen to your eldest uncle's critique."

Li Luo: "..."

His father's devilish whisper echoed in his ears. Li Luo swept his gaze over his eldest uncle's family and subconsciously took half a step back.

His hand tightened on the doorknob. He took a deep breath to keep his body from trembling.

The thought of them reading his novel sent a wave of sorrow through Li Luo. He suddenly felt that in this vast world, there was no place for him.

This home.

He might as well not have come back!

(End of this chapter)
